summary: This class explores the traditional practice of avoiding the use of shoes belonging to a deceased person. Rabbi Harari examines the origins of this custom in Sefer Hasidim, discusses various rationales provided by later authorities, and addresses whether these concerns apply to modern clothing and footwear.
questions: Is it forbidden to wear the shoes of a family member who has passed away?
Does the prohibition against wearing a deceased person's shoes apply to all types of clothing?
Is there a difference between leather shoes and other types of footwear regarding this custom?
If I am worried about this custom, can I sanitize the items to make them permissible?
Should I destroy the shoes of a deceased person to prevent others from using them?
